text:
andrew: quick FYI, after the slim-kernel rollout i'm seeing a 10-20% 99p bump for low-token fragmented requests. not universal, a slice of hosts.

maria: do we have a repro or flamegraph?

andrew: spike in host-side parse/serialize before batching. trace shows many small write syscalls instead of writev. KV cache evictions tick up with fragment count.

perf-bot: alert PERF-4801: 99p +17% on /v1/generate for requests <256 tokens and fragment_count>4 since deploy 3594990000.

ken: sounds like coalesce/writev fallout combined with kernel hint. hypothesis: slim kernels encourage mini-chunks upstream, reducing writev coalescing and scattering kvcache accesses.

sara: mitigation ideas: bump coalesce time for low-token routes (+1-2ms), add writev heuristic when kernel_hint=slim, or route high-frag flows away from slim.

andrew: ran a 5m canary adding +2ms coalesce for that route: write_calls/request dropped from ~4.0 -> ~1.6, 99p back near baseline, kvcache evictions reduced. cpu profile shows parse CPU falling ~20%.

maria: nice. plan: roll coalesce tweak to 50% for 1h, add telemetry counters (writev_calls, small_write_count) and a temporary routing rule to avoid slim for fragment_count>6.

ken: add a perf ticket to measure writev vs kvcache evictions (PERF-4802). also ensure long-sequence paths unaffected.

andrew: logging RUNTIME-3201 (coalesce canary), RUNTIME-3202 (routing temporary rule). will post rollout metrics.

sara: if coalesce tweak isn't sufficient we can pin shard affinity for hot routes or add micro-prefetch in kvcache for mini-chunks.

maria: thanks everyone, good triage.
